title: The New Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
paragraphs: Rathbone/Bruce-era Sherlock Holmes archive subset spanning selected surviving broadcasts from 1939 through May 1946. The series moved from NBC/Blue to Mutual, changed title in October 1943, and mixed direct Doyle adaptations with new radio stories built from Doyle characters/incidents.

GRH documents the program through NBC/Blue Bromo Quinine era (October 2, 1939 to March 1, 1942) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Mutual pre-rename era (May 7, 1943 to October 15, 1943) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]], and The New Adventures era (October 25, 1943 to May 27, 1946) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Arthur Conan Doyle (author on 37 recordings, creator on 14 recordings, and writer on 1 recording), Basil Rathbone (performer on 52 recordings), Nigel Bruce (performer on 50 recordings), Anthony Boucher (writer on 45 recordings, radio adaptor on 1 recording, and announcer on 1 recording), Denis Green (writer on 43 recordings, performer on 3 recordings, and radio adaptor on 1 recording), Edna Best (producer on 38 recordings), and Harry Bartell (announcer on 38 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), and [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include deduction and criminal investigation, murder and homicide, espionage, spies and state secrets, disguise and concealed identity, Professor Moriarty and organized criminal plots, and apparent supernatural mystery.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Sherlock Holmes as a long-running radio franchise, Wartime Holmes broadcasts, Sponsor-driven network continuity, and Doyle adaptation and radio expansion.

plain_text:
Rathbone/Bruce-era Sherlock Holmes archive subset spanning selected surviving broadcasts from 1939 through May 1946. The series moved from NBC/Blue to Mutual, changed title in October 1943, and mixed direct Doyle adaptations with new radio stories built from Doyle characters/incidents.

GRH documents the program through NBC/Blue Bromo Quinine era (October 2, 1939 to March 1, 1942) on NBC Radio Network, Mutual pre-rename era (May 7, 1943 to October 15, 1943) on Mutual Broadcasting System, and The New Adventures era (October 25, 1943 to May 27, 1946) on Mutual Broadcasting System.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Arthur Conan Doyle (author on 37 recordings, creator on 14 recordings, and writer on 1 recording), Basil Rathbone (performer on 52 recordings), Nigel Bruce (performer on 50 recordings), Anthony Boucher (writer on 45 recordings, radio adaptor on 1 recording, and announcer on 1 recording), Denis Green (writer on 43 recordings, performer on 3 recordings, and radio adaptor on 1 recording), Edna Best (producer on 38 recordings), and Harry Bartell (announcer on 38 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to Mutual Broadcasting System (broadcast on network), NBC Radio Network (broadcast on network), and Armed Forces Radio Service (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include deduction and criminal investigation, murder and homicide, espionage, spies and state secrets, disguise and concealed identity, Professor Moriarty and organized criminal plots, and apparent supernatural mystery.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Sherlock Holmes as a long-running radio franchise, Wartime Holmes broadcasts, Sponsor-driven network continuity, and Doyle adaptation and radio expansion.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include Lux Radio Theatre (8 shared credited people), The Halls of Ivy (4 shared credited people), The Whistler (7 shared credited people), Crime Classics (3 shared credited people), and Dr. Christian (2 shared credited people).
